The product is based on the INSPIRE elevation specification.
Grid data is available as ASCII grid.
Grid data is available as GML 3.2.1.
Contour data is available as GML 3.2.1.
Contour data is available as Esri shapefile.
Tiles are identified by the National Grid reference of their south-west corner.
GML features and geometries require unique identifiers.
Feature identifiers use an os.t5 tile-and-sequence structure.
Updates are supplied as whole-tile refreshes.
Sequential identifiers are regenerated after a tile update.
GML geometries use EPSG:27700 in an OGC URN.
The source terrain model is a triangulated irregular network.
The source TIN uses mass points.
Source editing occurs in a photogrammetric environment.
TIN triangles retain feature edges better than a regular grid.
Grid data is interpolated from the source TIN.
Contour data is interpolated from the source TIN.
Minimum coastal coverage extends to the low-water mark.
The outer edge of mapped inland-water land is captured.
The model should be free of false terrain spikes.
Major communication routes should be longitudinally smooth.
The grid GML contains metadata rather than the external height block.
Spatial height values are held in the ASCII grid file.
Each grid value is the mean height across a 5 metre pixel.
Heights are supplied to the nearest 0.01 metre.
The header gives south-west corner coordinates.
The supply includes a PRJ spatial-reference file.
The supply includes an asc.aux.xml styling file.
It uses the GML simple-features level-0 profile.
XML schemas validate GML format and content.
GML schemas can describe points, lines and polygons.
Spot heights are selected by an automated process.
The process selects the highest mass point inside a closed contour.
A selected point must differ from the enclosing contour by at least one metre.
Spot-height z values are rounded to one decimal place.
Grid heights are calculated at pixel centres.
Mean high and low water heights vary around the coast.
Tidal lines receive constant values based on each tile's average.
Tile averages are determined from local tide tables.
Tidal lines are used as heighted breaklines.
The breaklines keep grid and contour products consistent.
Adjacent coastal tiles can contain a small discrete tidal-height step.
OS Terrain 5 is supplied by download only.
It is available through the OS Data Hub.
It is also available through OS Orders.
The national grid set contains 10,579 tiles.
The national contour set contains 10,572 tiles.
National ZIP supplies are not encrypted.
The compressed national grid supply is approximately 16 GB.
The compressed national GML contour supply is approximately 2.6 GB.
The compressed national shapefile contour supply is approximately 2.5 GB.
Full-tile resupply is scheduled for January, April, July and October.
